title: PRD: Postmortem-derived canary scenarios + rollout gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Recent incidents (see postmortem links) exposed that our current canary/rollout harness is insufficiently representative of real failure modes. Manual canaries catch basic regressions but frequently miss compound scenarios observed in production (e.g., cached state loss + burst traffic + model quantization mismatch).

Goal: Define product requirements to capture, curate, and operationalize postmortem-derived canary scenarios that can be attached to model and infra rollouts. These scenarios should be runnable automatically during staged rollouts and must produce deterministic, measurable pass/fail signals (latency percentiles, error rates, and quality drift metrics). The PRD covers data model for scenarios, Console UX, API/CLI for attaching scenarios to rollout policies, acceptance thresholds, privacy constraints, and rollout gating behavior (automatic aborts and fallback triggers).
acceptance_criteria: Import: Product must be able to import at least five historical incident traces as candidate scenarios (traffic + metadata) into the Console as 'postmortem scenarios'
Simulation: For each scenario, the platform can replay traffic in staging and collect latency P50/P95/P99, 5xx rate, and a quality-drift score computed by token-level similarity/regression harness

Gating: Rollout pipeline must allow attaching one or more postmortem scenarios to a rollout; a failing scenario (predefined threshold breach) will abort the rollout and trigger a canary rollback policy
Observability: Scenario runs must produce a per-scenario dashboard and a synthetic-verification entry in the rollout timeline in Console
Privacy: Imported scenarios must be scrubbed for PII; product prohibits importing traces marked with customer-controlled PII flags
Scale: Scenario execution latency footprint must not add more than 5% to rollout duration for standard model rollouts (measured on a 10% canary window)
Docs & Runbook: Runbook for on-call must include steps to respond to scenario failures and a checklist for converting new postmortem items into scenarios
E2E tests: Automated tests in CI that run a lightweight, deterministic scenario against a canary deployment and assert gating behavior
decisions: Scope: MVP will support synthetic replay in staging clusters only; production shadowing will be evaluated in v2
Data retention: Scenario payloads retained for 90 days by default with manual export option
Quality metric: Use a configurable combination of token-level embedding cosine similarity + domain-specific heuristic score; default for PRD is embedding similarity with 0.92 threshold
Access control: Only customers with Dedicated or Private plans can create scenario imports containing sensitive metadata; hosted imports must be scrubbed
Chargeback: Scenario runs for internal verification are free; customer-initiated large-scale replays may be billable (follow pricing guidance)
implementation_notes: Backend: new 'scenario' archive object (metadata + compressed trace) stored in bucket with IAM controls; attachable to rollout via rollout_config.scenarios[]
Runner: lightweight traffic replayer that supports rate shaping, header injection, and temporal spacing to recreate spike patterns
Metrics: extend rollout telemetry to emit per-scenario metrics and a unified pass/fail boolean to the rollout event stream
Console: UI panel to browse scenarios, preview summary stats, and attach/detach from rollouts; include a 'replay in staging' button
Privacy: integrate with data-scrubbing lib used by incident ingestion; expose an audit trail for scenario imports
Testing: include an integration harness that seeds a deterministic scenario and asserts the abort path when thresholds are exceeded
